title: Generic clopenness of a section component over a base-point closure
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes (locally of finite type and quasi-compact as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]), and let $\sigma:T\to P$ be a section with $g\circ\sigma=\operatorname{id}_T$. For every point $y\in T$ there is an ambient open $V\subseteq T$ containing $y$ such that the subset of $g^{-1}(V\cap\overline{\{y\}})$ consisting of points $q$ in the connected component of $\sigma(g(q))$ in the topological fibre $g^{-1}(\{g(q)\})$ is open and closed in the subspace topology. No noetherian, separatedness, flatness or smoothness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 055N, using Tag 055M; ambient-open and closed-immersion topological formulation

proof.text: give the closure of y its reduced closed subscheme structure. Base change the morphism and section to this integral scheme; Tag 055M identifies the section locus with the inverse image of the original locus. The generic fibre is a finite type scheme over a field, hence noetherian. Its section component and its complement are clopen. Take their closures in the total space. Tag 054Y permits shrinking the integral base so these two closures cover the total space; Tag 054W permits further shrinking to make their intersection empty. The first closure is now clopen. Its generic fibre is connected and has the rational point supplied by the section, so it is geometrically connected by Tag 04KV. Tag 055G permits shrinking the base again so that all its fibres are geometrically connected. Intersect also with the inverse image under the section of the first closure; this open contains the generic point. Each fibre of the first closure is then a nonempty connected clopen subset of the whole fibre containing the section point, hence is precisely its connected component. This identifies the first closure with the section locus on the remaining open. A closed immersion and its base change are homeomorphisms onto their images, so the base-changed total space has the subspace topology on the inverse image of the closure of y. Express the remaining open of the closure of y as the intersection with an ambient open V of T. Since y is the generic point of its closure, V contains y. Transport clopenness along the indicated homeomorphism to obtain the displayed subtype statement.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_section_component_clopen {P T : Scheme.{u}} (g : P ⟶ T)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    (σ : T ⟶ P) (hσ : σ ≫ g = 𝟙 T) (y : T) :
    ∃ V : Set T, IsOpen V ∧ y ∈ V ∧
      IsClopen {q : g ⁻¹' (V ∩ closure {y}) |
        (q : P) ∈ connectedComponentIn (g ⁻¹' {g (q : P)}) (σ (g (q : P)))}
